PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer review and follow-up work.

Current state:
- Latest head implements the algorithm (not just occlusion foundation): 17 coverage-engine files, worker, UI, tests. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs by bitset union with quality/contribution tie-breakers; not greedy first-origin selection.
- Shared coarse-to-fine engine: 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches.
- Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, both search modes.
- Recent patch aligned runtime shader to optimizer: removed stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF=6.0 / projectedConfidence assertion; now asserts projectedQualityAt, dominance bias (blendMode==2/3 ? 1.15 : 1.0), no projectedConfidence. multiOriginInteraction.test.ts: 36/36 passed.
- Full suite just ran: 42 test files, 371 tests passed; lint (tsc --noEmit) and build (vite) both passed. Notable slow tests: projectionCoverage.test.ts 10 tests ~39.2s (runs both optimizer modes on 100k+ triangle indexed fixture), occlusion/projected WebGL readback tests ~4s each.

Review verdict (from user review of this push):
- Algorithm architecture for normal graybox sets: 8/10
- Correctness of two search modes: 7.5/10
- Readiness for complex imported sets: 4/10
- Overall: promising, not production-ready to merge yet.

Blockers / required changes:
1. Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates. Extractor stores entire object AABB as obstacle; clearance is distance from origin to AABB, points inside AABB get 0 and are rejected. A single imported SceneObject whose AABB encloses the room rejects all sensible origins. Fix: use actual geometry clearance (camera sphere/capsule vs nearby triangles) via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance / sphere intersection / shapecast; obstacle bounds per connected mesh or spatial cluster, not per imported set object. Add regression test: one imported object containing room floor/walls/empty interior.
2. Geometry representation won't scale to heavy imports. Every triangle expanded into 3 Vec3 world-space arrays + normals + IDs + area; for 3M triangles minimum packed ~144MB, actual JS objects/arrays/64-bit numbers several times larger, then structured-cloned into worker with postMessage (another huge copy). BVH recursively sorts/slices JS index arrays; raycasts allocate temporary 3-element arrays → GC pressure. Fix: compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals? Float32Array, meshRanges Uint32Array, transforms Float32Array), transfer ArrayBuffers instead of cloning nested objects; BVH via three-mesh-bvh, flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries; avoid expanding indexed vertices into 3 world-space vertex arrays per triangle.
3. Geometry extraction still blocks main thread. Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to worker, so worker only offloads optimizer, not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, structured cloning. On complex models app may freeze before worker reports first progress. Fix: move extraction into worker or chunk it and yield between meshes.
4. "Apply to selected panorama pair" is conceptually wrong. UI writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference(primary/secondaryPanoId, {origin}). Changing metadata doesn't transform the image; it projects old pixels from wrong point, ruining alignment. Correct workflow: fixed-first — preserve existing panorama+origin, move next capture origin to B, render new graybox panorama, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin; joint — create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, associate each result with its actual origin. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses different fine sample bank generated with seed+1. Same result shows both and computes reachable efficiency → can show Combined 83%, Reachable upper bound 80%, Reachable captured 100% (clamp hides impossible ratio but doesn't repair incompatible estimates). Also fixed-first reachable set calculated before arbitrary first origin evaluated, so fixed first origin not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union. Can keep separate coarse/fine search banks internally, but reported metrics must be evaluated on one shared final bank.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so even identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. "Four-level refinement" not truly iterative. For every seed, all offsets generated around original seed (seed ± spacing/2, /4, /8, /16); does not select best half-step result and center quarter-step search around new result. Useful multiresolution neighborhood sample, but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in plan. True refinement loop would update center after every level.
8. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y. On sloped terrain/multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height → origin floats meters above new floor. Fix per offset: find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
9. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; when both panoramas visible, actual shader still blends only by distance. Optimizer may prefer source for frontal angle while runtime favors closer but more grazing source → optimized coverage result and visible result don't fully agree. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. (Recent patch moved toward this with projectedQualityAt + dominance modes.)

Testing gaps (absent but dangerous):
1. One large imported object containing entire room.
2. 100k+ triangle performance fixture (note: projectionCoverage.test.ts now runs both optimizer modes on 100k+ indexed fixture, ~39s).
3. reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant.
4. Fixed-first candidate separation.
5. Sloped and multilevel floors.
6. Existing panorama origins remaining immutable.
7. Candidate generation inside concave imported geometry.
No GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head, so reported test suite not independently enforced in CI.
